claims.text: Near-equiatomic FeCoNi has a face-centered-cubic structure.
The proposed near-equiatomic FeCoNi composition has configurational entropy of at least 1.0R.
A minor substitutional Al addition can produce a near-equiatomic FeCoNiAl alloy while preserving configurational entropy of at least 1.0R.
Adding Al to FeCoNi will induce partial chemical ordering.
Adding Al to FeCoNi will form nanoscale secondary phases.
The Al-induced ordered precipitates or secondary phases will occur within a mostly disordered fcc matrix.
Al tends to promote partial chemical ordering when substituted into this alloy.
Al-induced ordering creates nanoscale chemical or structural heterogeneity.
The resulting nanoscale heterogeneity acts as pinning centers for magnetic domain walls.
Domain-wall pinning impedes domain-wall motion and thereby increases coercivity.
FeCoNiAl will have a higher coercive field than identically processed equiatomic FeCoNi.
FeCoNiAl will retain high saturation magnetization after the proposed intervention.
Tailored annealing can encourage incipient ordering without causing full phase separation.
Significant changes in composition or processing may cause uncontrolled phase formation and eliminate the anticipated coercivity increase.

contradictions.description: The intervention simultaneously describes Al as a minor addition and the resulting four-element FeCoNiAl alloy as near-equiatomic or as maintaining overall equiatomic composition. A genuinely minor Al fraction is not approximately equiatomic with Fe, Co, and Ni unless the intended meaning of equiatomic is restricted to the original three elements.
